title: Docs claimed that ``assert`` is a function defined in ase.test, it is neither.
body:
Docs claimed that ``assert`` is a function defined in ase.test, it is neither.
(just a bit of nit-picking)

author: schiotz

comments.author: yuzie007
comments.body:
Instead of the explicit link
```rst
they are, :keyword:`assert` it!
```
(or `:py:keyword:`) probably works and links to the same Python website.
comments.label_reasoning: The comment suggests using a specific RST directive syntax for linking to Python documentation, which is a documentation formatting improvement.

comments.author: ajjackson
comments.body:
I have just tried this and indeed it works. I think with

```:keyword:`assert` ```

we also do not need the following few lines explaining what it does; Python docs + the Example should be sufficient.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Suggests using :keyword:`assert` or :py:keyword: instead of an explicit link — a concrete change to the RST markup.

comments.author: ajjackson
comments.body:
How about

```suggestion:-14+0
**Replicable results**
    Even if a calculation makes it to the end without crashing, you can never
    be too sure that the numerical results are consistent. Don't just assume
    they are, :keyword:`assert` it!

Example::
```
comments.label_reasoning: The comment provides a concrete suggestion to rewrite documentation text in tests.rst, improving clarity and proper use of RST keyword linking.

comments.author: schiotz
comments.body: Yes, if that works. I did not know the :keyword: role :-)

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Provides a specific code suggestion block with concrete documentation changes.
